newsitem.title: USA: NYSE June 23-27 program trading averages 20.6 pct.
newsitem.headline: NYSE June 23-27 program trading averages 20.6 pct.

text.p: The New York Stock Exchange said Thursday that program trading for the week of June 23-27 amounted to 108.4 million shares a day, or 20.6 percent of the exchange's average daily volume of 527.2 million shares.
In the previous week, program trading accounted for 25.1 percent of average daily volume, or 132.7 million shares a day.
The exchange said buy programs accounted for 9.7 percent, and sell programs accounted for 10.9 percent pf the average daily volume of program trades.
In all markets, program trading averaged 153.5 million shares a day during the week, the NYSE said.

Of the five member firms reporting the most program activity on the New York Stock Exchange, BNP Securities, Morgan Stanley, Natwest, Susquehanna Brokerage Services and Salomon Brothers each executed all or most of their program activity for customers, as agent or facilitator.

Program trading executed by firms as agent, for non-member customers, amounted to 78.2 percent during the week, while volume executed as principal, for their own accounts, amounted to 20.5 percent of program volume.

Between June 23 and June 27, 17.6 percent of program trading volume executed by NYSE member firms was related to index arbitrage, while another 1.1 percent involved other derivative product-related strategies.
Program trading encompasses trading strategies involving the sale or purchase of a basket of at least 15 stocks with a value of $1 million or more the exchange said.
